 SOUTHCOM Kills Five Narco-Terrorists in Pacific, Pushing Campaign Toll Past 230
 SOFX Editor Staff Staff Writer 
 Oct 27, 2026 
4 min read 
 Share this article 
 (Screengrab via SOUTHCOM) 
 Takeaways Up Front
 1. SOUTHCOM said Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere struck a go-fast vessel in the eastern Pacific on October 27, killing five it described as narco-terrorists.
 2. The lethal strike came four days after the Coast Guard interdicted a suspected vessel and detained its crew alive.
 3. A Pentagon inspector general review of the campaign’s targeting process remains open as the reported toll tops 230.
 U.S. Southern Command said Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere carried out a lethal strike on a go-fast boat in the eastern Pacific on October 27, killing five people the command described as narco-terrorists moving drugs along established smuggling routes.
 The command released an unclassified video of the strike and said confirmed intelligence tied the vessel to narco-trafficking. It did not make that intelligence public or say what the boat was carrying.
 On October 27, under the direction of #SOUTHCOM, Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere executed a lethal, kinetic strike on a go-fast vessel operating along established narco-trafficking routes in the Eastern Pacific. Confirmed intelligence revealed the vessel’s active involvement in narco-trafficking. The operation killed five narco-terrorists. @DeptofWar @SecWar
— U.S. Southern Command (@Southcom) October 27, 2026 
 A Strike and an Interdiction Days Apart 
 Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere executed the operation under Southern Command’s direction, striking what the military calls a go-fast boat, a small, high-speed craft commonly used to run narcotics. Gen. Francis L. Donovan commands Southern Command, and Maj. Gen. Kevin Jarrard leads the task force.
 Four days earlier, on October 23, Southern Command said the Coast Guard interdicted a suspected trafficking vessel and apprehended those aboard. In earlier encounters, crews were removed before their boats were sunk, producing no deaths. The two approaches, a lethal strike and a boarding that takes a crew alive, have run in parallel through the campaign.
 Dismantling narco-terrorist networks in the Caribbean.
— U.S. Southern Command (@Southcom) October 25, 2026 
 The Washington Office on Latin America, which tracks the strikes, counts 243 people killed including Tuesday’s operation. Adam Isacson, an analyst at the group, said it was “the 6th lethal boat strike in the past 4 months.”
 A Reorganized Command and an Open Review 
 The campaign began on September 2, 2025, in the Caribbean and expanded into the eastern Pacific that October. Trackers that follow it put the toll above 230 across more than 70 strikes, with counts differing by how each group tallies operations.
 The task force behind the recent strikes is new. Southern Command activated Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere in early August, replacing Operation Southern Spear and describing it as the command’s action arm. Strikes resumed on August 23 after a pause of more than two months, the longest since the campaign began.
 The Trump administration has said the United States is in an armed conflict with cartels it has designated as terrorist organizations, a rationale set out in a classified Justice Department opinion.
 Legal experts and rights groups say the strikes could amount to extrajudicial killings because they have targeted people who did not pose an immediate threat, and the administration has not published definitive evidence tying the boats to trafficking.
 Centers for Disease Control and Prevention data show no significant decrease in fatal overdoses since the strikes began. Congress has voted repeatedly on resolutions to halt the strikes, and none has passed.
 What’s Next: A Pentagon inspector general review, opened in a May 11 memo , is examining whether Southern Command followed the approved six-step targeting process before the strikes. Its findings have not been released, and lawmakers on the armed services committees have pressed for unedited strike video.
 Sources
 Army Times , Natalie Oliverio, “SOUTHCOM replaces Southern Spear with Western Hemisphere task force targeting criminal networks,” Aug. 6, 2026 .
 Stars and Stripes , “US Forces Strike Suspected Drug Boat in Eastern Pacific, Killing 5,” Oct. 27, 2026 .
 Al Jazeera , Brian Osgood, “US says it killed five people in strike on alleged drug boat,” Oct. 27, 2026 .

 CNN (via KRDO ), Logan Schiciano, “Pentagon watchdog evaluating US operations involving strikes on alleged drug boats,” May 19, 2026 .
